newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Former Venezuela coup leader launches election bid.
newsitem.headline: Former Venezuela coup leader launches election bid.

text.p: The leader of a bloody army coup attempt that shook Venezuela's democracy five years ago announced on Tuesday a formal bid for presidential elections next year.
Accompanied by about 2,000 vocal flag-waving supporters, retired Lt. Col. Hugo Chavez registered his Fifth Republic Movement (MVR) with electoral authorities to participate in the Dec. 1998 vote.
The new political movement would attract the majority of Venezuelans who have lost faith in traditional political parties, Chavez said.
"MVR will serve as a platform for the creation of government of patriotic reconstruction demanded by the country," he said.
Chavez led a failed rebellion on Feb. 4, 1992, and was jailed for two years until President Rafael Caldera pardoned the rebellious officers shortly after assuming power.
His movement was registered simultaneously on Tuesday with regional electoral authorities in Venezuela's 22 states.
Chavez became the first political leader to proclaim his presidential candidacy officially. Former beauty queen Irene Saez, Venezuela's most popular politician, has hinted she will also run.
Political analysts say Chavez is not a serious political threat but his populist message laced with leftist rhetoric is effective among the poor.
